title: What is digital forensics?
quick: Digital forensics is the careful identification, collection, preservation, examination, analysis and reporting of data from digital devices, done so that its integrity is protected and others can check and repeat the findings.

sections.title: What it covers
text: Digital forensics applies scientific methods to digital evidence. Digital evidence is any data that may help show what happened, such as files, messages, logs and network traffic. The work is used in criminal cases, company investigations, incident response and civil disputes.
Procedures and laws differ by country and agency. Follow your lab's own procedure.

sections.title: What makes it forensic
text: Many people can read files from a drive. Forensic work adds rules. You keep the original unchanged, you write down every step, and you show that your results can be repeated by another trained person.
The aim is to find facts and report them fairly. You do not decide guilt. You describe what the data shows and how sure you are.

sections.title: Main stages
text: Most guides describe four stages: collection, examination, analysis and reporting. Each stage must protect the integrity of the data, which means the data stays unchanged and can be shown to be unchanged. The next topics explain these stages in detail.

sections.title: Skills a student needs
text: You need to understand file systems, operating systems and how apps store data. You also need clear note taking and writing. A tool only shows data. The examiner must understand and explain it.

compare.title: Digital forensics and general IT support
rows: Find and report facts about past events
Data is often changed or repaired

example: A company finds that a laptop was used to send confidential files. An examiner makes a copy of the laptop drive, checks the copy with a hash, and studies only the copy. The report lists what was found, the steps taken and the limits of the findings.
mistakes: Believing that forensics means only recovering deleted files.
Opening files on the original device instead of working on a copy.
Writing opinions as if they were facts.
Relying on one tool result without understanding it.
Skipping notes because the work seems simple.

terms.meaning: Data stored or sent in digital form that may help in an investigation.
The state of data being complete and unchanged.
The person who carries out the forensic work.
A trace left by a user or system activity, such as a log entry or a browser history record.

exam.q: What is digital forensics in one sentence?
exam.a: It is the careful collection, examination, analysis and reporting of digital data in a way that protects its integrity and can be repeated and checked.
It lets another examiner repeat the work and reach the same result, and it shows how the evidence was handled.
